hook: A very short entry about a small figure made of shadow. It takes a minute to read, so pay attention to the containment setup, which tells you most of what you need to know before the description does.
whyItMatters: It is a clean example of the one-rule creature: a single trigger and a single, total consequence. The image of a cage flooded with light from every side is memorable on its own. Its brevity works in its favor, since nothing is explained beyond what is needed to make the rule stick.
thingsToNotice:
The reflective suits and the warning not to stand in front of working lamps are the real story; the procedures imply what happens long before it is stated. The rule, once spelled out, is total: whatever casts a shadow on it gets pounced on, swallowed into the smoky shroud, and vanishes without a trace, so a single burnt-out lamp or a careless step in front of a spotlight could mean losing a person.

Its size, about that of a small child, is mentioned once and never commented on, which makes it more unsettling. The remark that nothing has been found beneath its shroud, without ruling anything out, is a neat loose end. The closing pointer to a separate document for higher clearance leaves the sense that this file is deliberately incomplete.
